summary.headline: Prioritise paid service pilots over speculative SaaS; cyber hygiene is the strongest evidence-led test today.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup for small UK businesses.
summary.why_now: The live GOV.UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 provides a current UK business-risk signal. It does not prove willingness to pay, so validate with buyers before scaling. Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2025/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2025

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup
top_opportunities.description: A bounded, non-intrusive service covering MFA and backup checks, account recovery, practical phishing response and a prioritized action register; refer specialist work to qualified providers.
top_opportunities.why_now: The UK government's Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 is a timely public risk signal. Incident prevalence is not evidence of local buying intent, which still requires paid validation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional-services firms, charities and owner-managed businesses without in-house IT/security staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£900 for training, insurance/legal review, demo materials and basic tooling; only offer work within competence and cover.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through paid readiness reviews and referrals; validate first.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium: quarterly checks and staff refreshers could support a retainer if clients see value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical implementation and automation fit; security competence, trust and scope discipline are essential.
risks: Do not claim certification, guaranteed protection or perform intrusive tests without competence and written authorization.
Trust barrier and established MSP competition; survey incident data does not establish service purchasing.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best to test as a tightly scoped readiness service; do not build SaaS first.

top_opportunities.name: SME workflow automation implementation
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope automation of a repetitive workflow such as enquiry triage, appointment reminders, document intake or CRM updates, with human review where needed.
top_opportunities.why_now: Existing tools make small pilots inexpensive, but this run found no reliable evidence of demand for generic AI consulting. Sell a measurable operational outcome instead.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-operated service firms and small professional practices with repetitive admin.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 for demos, API usage and basic insurance/legal review.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks through a paid workflow audit and implementation; not guaranteed.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential through monitoring and improvement retainers, subject to proving value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for an engineer integrating existing tools and measuring time saved.
risks: Generic AI positioning is crowded and undifferentiated.
Fragile integrations, scope creep and personal-data handling create delivery risk.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell a paid pilot in one niche before building reusable software.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business lead response and booking service
top_opportunities.description: Set up enquiry capture, missed-call follow-up, booking and lead reminders for one local service niche using existing tools.
top_opportunities.why_now: It ties implementation to bookings and revenue, but this run did not retrieve independent live evidence of the size of the local unmet need; test directly with businesses.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, clinics or other appointment-led businesses with slow enquiry response.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,200 using existing booking, messaging and website tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks with a paid setup and pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential through monthly management, contingent on retention and measurable results.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good engineering fit; sales and local prospecting are likely constraints.
risks: Lead attribution and low enquiry volumes can weaken the value case.
Messaging consent, deliverability and platform rules need attention.
top_opportunities.verdict: Test one vertical with a short pilot and a baseline response/booking metric.

top_opportunities.name: Invoice-chasing workflow setup for small B2B firms
top_opportunities.description: Configure invoice reminders, overdue escalation and a basic receivables view in the client's existing accounting workflow.
top_opportunities.why_now: Late payment is a plausible operational pain, but this run did not retrieve a fresh reliable quantitative source. Validate pain and tool gaps with prospective customers.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small agencies, consultancies and subcontractors invoicing other businesses.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–4 weeks; depends on access to decision-makers and paid pilot conversion.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium through maintenance and reporting, though existing accounting software may suffice.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong integration fit; avoid financial advice and protect access to sensitive data.
risks: Accounting platforms may already solve the problem adequately.
Financial data access requires strong permissions, trust and security.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell setup only where customers confirm a specific gap; avoid a standalone app initially.

top_opportunities.name: Niche website care and conversion service
top_opportunities.description: Maintain and improve websites for one local-business vertical: speed, forms, booking flow, accessibility basics and monthly reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Can produce project revenue quickly using existing tools; this run did not retrieve direct current evidence quantifying unmet demand, so niche-level validation is essential.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small local businesses relying on outdated or poorly converting websites.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for hosting, monitoring, templates and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through fixed-price audits and repairs.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium through maintenance retainers if clients value ongoing work.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical fit; sales and differentiation may be harder than delivery.
risks: Crowded commodity market with DIY and agency competition.
Unclear content responsibilities and approvals can delay delivery.
top_opportunities.verdict: Use as a productized service only with a clear niche and measurable conversion improvement.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene and phishing-readiness setup
best_pick.why_it_wins: It pairs a current official risk signal with service delivery that needs no custom product investment. Evidence is directional; validate buyer demand and competence fit before proceeding.
validation_plan: Interview 8 local small-business owners and 3 independent IT/MSP providers about existing controls, unmet needs and referral boundaries.
Offer three paid fixed-scope reviews; proceed only if customers pay and a qualified security practitioner validates scope and checklist.
best_pick.first_offer: A fixed-price Cyber Hygiene Baseline: account/MFA and backup review, prioritized action list and assisted setup of agreed low-risk improvements. Exclude certification, penetration testing and security guarantees.
best_pick.mvp: A documented checklist, authorized evidence review, concise action report and optional quarterly follow-up; use established tools and do not store client credentials.
customer_types: Small professional-services firms without in-house IT
best_pick.do_today: Read the GOV.UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025, draft a one-page scope and contact three local business owners plus one MSP; verify qualifications, insurance and scope before offering security advice.
